scientific_question: Does serial-bending refinement approach the fixed Stage 3.10 GVS reference?

conclusion.interpretation: All six primary errors decrease at every refinement, as do every component COM/position error, the total mass error and aggregate tendon-length error. Geometry, COM and gravity show approximately first-order reduction; stiffness and mass show second-order reduction on the finer meshes. This supports finite serial discretization as a large contributor to the Stage 3.7–3.9 mismatch under the required integrated-curvature mapping. The single coarse tendon-length reversal does not overturn the consistent multi-quantity trend.
conclusion.recommendation: Define a minimal cross-model equivalence contract and select practical fidelity levels from measured cost versus error, retaining per-tendon checks; no universal cell count is established here.

suspected_nonconvergent_mechanism.primary_metrics: None shows a persistent plateau or worsening trend in the tested range.
suspected_nonconvergent_mechanism.status: Plausible coarse-grid explanation, not established nonconvergence or a demonstrated cause.
